implementation.argument_surface: receiver in ECX (aliased into ESI at 0x00641fd4 and never read again after 0x00642045); NO ordinary stack argument. The argument count is machine-fixed twice over: both exits are a bare `RET` (0x00642059 and 0x0064206c, bytes c3) with no immediate, and the epilogue pops EDI then ESI and adds 0xc back (0x00642067..0x00642069), which lands ESP exactly on the entry value. The record agrees: stack_arguments.derived_slots 0, observed_slots 0, cleanup.bytes 0, cleanup.side "caller".
implementation.receiver_model: a struct whose only content is an opaque byte run; every receiver access in the body is a displacement (0x00, 0x08, 0x3c) and no member is named, because the machine-derived receiver record is bounds_only with offsets [0, 8, 60] and says nothing about which member is which. The three sub-objects the body reaches (the service root, the service, the resolved handle) are opaque runs sized to the last byte this set touches, with the callee-side offsets recorded as values in the header's comment rather than as members.
implementation.dispatch_model: two two-level virtual dispatches, both modelled as a table word read from an object's own +0x00 and a slot word read from THAT: slot displacement 0x90 (index 36) on the receiver, taken with the receiver in ECX and one stack word (the address of the body's 8-byte frame object); slot displacement 0x04 (index 1) on the resolved handle, taken with the handle in ECX and no stack word. Both are typed from the CALL SITE, which is what the machine fixes, and neither is attributed to a class: the same slot holds 0x00641fd0 itself in the table at 0x01462764 and 0x006417d0 in the table at 0x01489090.
implementation.dependency_note: the three direct callees are declared extern in the package header and defined as observers in the package's own model test; no other package's header is included and no other package's file was read for this reconstruction except for shape comparison. 0x0067cb30, 0x00613860 and 0x00612f50 are not owned by this package, and this package asserts nothing about them beyond what their own instruction bytes fix (terminator form, stack-argument shape, argument identity).

mechanics.body_shape: read the receiver's own +0x3c word; if it is nonzero return it unchanged. Otherwise seed an 8-byte frame object with the sentinel 0xffffffff in both words, dispatch the receiver's own table slot +0x90 with that object's address, fetch a global through 0x0067cb30 and read the service word at its +0x5c, ask 0x00613860 about the receiver's +0x08 word, hand the two frame words (re-read after the dispatch) plus the address of a third frame word and a literal zero to 0x00612f50, and then -- on BOTH of that callee's arms -- take a two-level acquire at slot +0x04 of whatever it left behind. The exit word is the cached word, the resolved handle, or zero.

frame_resolution.method: one linear walk of ESP through all 62 instructions, settling the stack after every call with that callee's OWN ret immediate: the slot +0x90 dispatch pops its one word (a __thiscall member function is the only reading under which the two frame reads at 0x0064201d and 0x00642021 land on the 8-byte object rather than on an argument word), 0x00613860 pops 4 (`C2 04 00`) and 0x00612f50 pops 16 (`C2 10 00`). Entry ESP is 0 in the walk; the walk ends at 0, so the frame balances exactly.
frame_resolution.corroboration: three independent agreements. (1) 0x00642027 forms ECX with LEA ECX,[ESP+0xc] at ESP = entry-24, i.e. entry-12, and 0x00642030 stores 0 at [ESP+0x18] with ESP = entry-36, i.e. the same entry-12; the address taken and the word zeroed are provably the same word. (2) At 0x0064203d, with ESP = entry-20, [ESP+0x0] is entry-20 (the saved EDI), [ESP+0x4] is entry-16 (the saved ESI) and [ESP+0x8] is entry-12 -- the three words a 12-byte frame ends with, in the order the pushes made them. (3) The epilogue POP EDI / POP ESI / ADD ESP,0xc returns ESP to the entry value, so a frame that did not balance would have to be repaired somewhere, and nothing in the listing repairs it.

slots.entry-4: the SECOND word of the 8-byte frame object; written -1 at 0x00641fe9, handed to the slot +0x90 dispatch by address, re-read at 0x0064201d into EDX and passed as the SECOND stack argument of 0x00612f50
slots.entry-8: the FIRST word of that object; written -1 at 0x00641fe5, its address is what 0x00641ff5 hands to the dispatch, re-read at 0x00642021 into EAX and passed as the FIRST stack argument of 0x00612f50
slots.entry-12: the out-slot: its address is 0x00612f50's third argument, it is zeroed at 0x00642030 immediately before that call, and it is read back at 0x0064203d

frame_resolution.corroboration_of_the_pair: the 8-byte object is ONE object, not two words: 0x00641ff5 forms a single address (entry-8) with a LEA and hands THAT one pointer to the dispatch, and the two later reads are at entry-8 and entry-4. There is no second LEA anywhere in the body, so nothing else could be the pair's address.

receiver_displacement.0x00: read at 0x00641fed (MOV EAX,[ESI]); it is the first level of the slot +0x90 dispatch -- the receiver's LEADING word is its table pointer
receiver_displacement.0x08: read at 0x0064200e (MOV EAX,[ESI+0x8]) and pushed at 0x00642011 as 0x00613860's only stack argument; passed by value, never dereferenced by this body
receiver_displacement.0x3c: read at 0x00641fd6 (MOV EAX,[ESI+0x3c]), tested at 0x00641fd9 (TEST EAX,EAX) and branched on at 0x00641fdb (JNZ 0x00642068); the value left in EAX is the return value of that path

mechanics.receiver_writes: NONE. The complete 62-instruction listing contains no store whose destination is a receiver-relative operand, and abi_derived.receiver.written_through is 0. The three stores in the body are 0x00641fe5 and 0x00641fe9 (the two frame words) and 0x00642030 (the out-slot), all to the body's own frame. The model test byte-compares the receiver's whole 0x40-byte run before and after three calls and after the cached path.
mechanics.control_flow: SEVEN conditional branches, all with absolute targets inside the recovered body span 0x00641fd0..0x0064206c: JNZ 0x00642068 (0x00641fdb), JZ 0x00642065 (0x00642000, 0x0064200c, 0x0064201b, 0x0064205c), JZ 0x0064205a (0x00642043) and JZ 0x00642052 (0x00642049). The count was taken from the listing and confirmed by the validator, which counted the same seven. There is no unconditional jump, no loop and no backward branch; the only other transfer out of an instruction is the three indirect calls. The graph is therefore a tree: five tests, four of which can fail to the shared null exit 0x00642065, one fast path at 0x00642068 that returns a word, and a two-armed tail whose arms differ only in the exit word.
mechanics.gate_order_is_fixed: the order in the listing is +0x3c, then the slot +0x90 dispatch, then the service word, then 0x00613860, then 0x00612f50. A reconstruction that reached 0x0067cb30 before the dispatch, or 0x00613860 before the service check, would be a different function: the model test pins the whole transfer sequence as a single ordered list, so a reordering fails it.
mechanics.the_acquire_runs_on_both_arms: 0x00642043 splits on 0x00612f50's byte, and BOTH arms contain the same two-level acquire (0x0064204b/0x0064204d/0x00642050 on the true arm, 0x0064205e/0x00642060/0x00642063 on the false arm). The only difference between the arms is the exit word: 0x00642053 moves the handle into EAX, 0x00642065 zeroes it. The duplication is carried in the original and is carried in this model rather than factored into a helper the listing does not have. Case G of the model test is the one that pins it: 0x00612f50 returns zero AND leaves a handle, and the acquire must still happen.
mechanics.byte_tests_are_not_equality: three of the gates are `TEST AL,AL` / `JZ` (0x00641ffe, 0x00642019, 0x00642041), so nonzero falls through and the values 0x02 through 0xff are all TRUE. The model test drives 0x80 through the dispatch and through 0x00613860 for exactly this reason.
mechanics.globals: none in the BODY. No one of the 62 instructions names a data-segment address. The nearest global is the one 0x0067cb30 reads, and that address is recorded here and in the header rather than in the reconstruction's function span, because a reconstruction that named a data address its own body does not contain would be making a claim the machine does not make.

direct_call_1.convention: not decidable, and not claimed: the whole callee is six bytes -- `A1 70 CC 5F 01 C3`, i.e. `MOV EAX,ds:0x15fcc70; RET` -- with no stack argument, a bare `RET` and no read of ECX. The header declares it cdecl because it demonstrably takes no receiver; the body passes nothing and reads nothing but the return.
direct_call_1.arguments: none. The body does not set up ECX or the stack for this call, and ECX at that point holds whatever the slot +0x90 dispatch left in it, which is why the callee must not be read as a member function.
direct_call_1.return: a pointer in EAX, used once: `MOV EDI,[EAX+0x5c]` at 0x00642007. The word at that +0x5c is the service, and it is null-tested at 0x0064200a.
direct_call_1.callee_record: no metadata record for this address; its shape was read from its own six image bytes

direct_call_2.convention: __thiscall (the callee ends `C2 04 00` at 0x6138a1 and takes its receiver in ECX at 0x613861), so the callee owns the one argument word
direct_call_2.arguments: one stack word, the dword the body read at the receiver's +0x08 (0x0064200e, pushed at 0x00642011), passed BY VALUE; the callee reads it at its own entry+4 (0x613885) and compares it UNSIGNED against the leading word of an array element (0x613889 `CMP ECX,[EAX]` / 0x61388b `JB`). ECX is the service from the root's +0x5c, not the receiver.
direct_call_2.return: a byte normalised to {0, 1} (0x61389a `SETNE DL`, 0x61389e `MOV AL,DL`), tested for non-zero by 0x00642019. The model test returns 0x80, which the body must read as true.
direct_call_2.callee_record: no metadata record for this address; its 68-byte body was read from the image

direct_call_3.convention: __thiscall (the callee ends `C2 10 00` on both exits, 0x612fad and 0x61300f, and takes its receiver in ECX at 0x612f52), so the callee owns all four argument words
direct_call_3.arguments: four words pushed right to left, so the callee's argument order is: FIRST the frame object's first word (re-read from entry-8 at 0x00642021), SECOND the frame object's second word (re-read from entry-4 at 0x0064201d), THIRD the address of the out-slot at entry-12 (formed by the LEA at 0x00642027), FOURTH the literal zero (0x00642025). The two data arguments are the values the slot +0x90 dispatch WROTE, not the sentinel the object was seeded with, because both are re-read from the frame after the dispatch returns. ECX is the service.
direct_call_3.return: a byte normalised to {0, 1} (`XOR AL,AL` at 0x612faa, `MOV AL,0x1` at 0x61300c), tested for non-zero by 0x00642041. It is NOT the handle: the handle is the separate word read from entry-12 at 0x0064203d, and the two are independent (case H of the model test returns a nonzero byte with a null handle).
direct_call_3.callee_record: no metadata record for this address; its 192-byte body was read from the image

indirect_call_1.receiver: the receiver itself: 0x00641ffa `MOV ECX,ESI`. Not the table word, and not the frame object.
indirect_call_1.stack: one word, the ADDRESS of the frame object (0x00641ff5 LEA / 0x00641ff9 PUSH), so the callee may write through it
indirect_call_1.return: a byte, tested for non-zero at 0x00641ffe
indirect_call_1.concrete_targets_in_the_image: the word at 0x01462764+0x90 is 0x00641fd0 -- this body -- and the word at 0x01489090+0x90 is 0x006417d0, so the same slot holds a different function in a different table and nothing here may assume the target is a different function than the receiver's own class would suggest. In the table at 0x013ff6ac the words at +0x8c and +0x90 are 0xffffffff and 0x3f000000, so that table is SHORTER than 0x90 bytes and +0x90 is not a slot of it; this body sits at its +0x38 (index 14), which is why the two indices are independent.

indirect_call_2.shape: two-level, slot displacement 0x04 (index 1), on the TRUE arm
indirect_call_2.receiver: the resolved handle, in ECX already (it was loaded at 0x0064203d and never moved)
indirect_call_2.return: dead: 0x00642053 overwrites EAX with the handle, so nothing observes it and the model declares it void

indirect_call_3.shape: two-level, slot displacement 0x04 (index 1), on the FALSE arm -- the same two instructions as indirect_call_2
indirect_call_3.why_it_matters: this is the site a reconstruction most easily loses, because the arm returns null. See mechanics.the_acquire_runs_on_both_arms.

mechanics.not_modelled: the dead return value of both acquire calls, and the prior contents of the out-slot (the machine never initialises it, so the model seeds it with a marker purely so that the store at 0x00642030 is observable, and the model test asserts the value AT THE CALL and never the value before it).

return_semantics.kind: a 32-bit word in EAX, with three different exits
return_semantics.value: the receiver's own +0x3c word when that is nonzero (0x00642068, which jumps into the shared epilogue and never overwrites EAX); the word 0x00612f50 left in the out-slot on its true arm (0x00642053 `MOV EAX,ESI`, with ESI loaded from that word at 0x00642045); and the literal 0 on all five failing gates (0x00642065 `XOR EAX,EAX`). The declared type is void* because that is the only single C type under which all three compile, and because the two arms that are not the cached path are unambiguously addresses. The record's own return claim is the string "integral_in_EAX" with abi_derived.return.register_class "integral" and type null, i.e. a claim about the register and the width and not about a C type.
return_semantics.ownership: The body acquires the handle it returns (slot +0x04) and never releases it; it also never releases on the arm where it discards the handle. Whether the callee at slot +0x04 is an acquire or a retain cannot be settled from the body, which shows the call and not its effect -- the slot is at index 1 of the handle's own table, which is a plausible place for either, and nothing in this repository names it.
return_semantics.lifetime: The 8-byte object and the out-slot are frame objects that die with the call. The out-slot's contents are the caller's problem: the body hands back an address it does not own a reference to beyond the one acquire it took.

unresolved_questions: What the receiver's +0x3c word IS is not established. The body tests it against zero, returns it unchanged and never dereferences it, so a cached pointer and a cached integer are indistinguishable here. It is the fastest path in the function, which is a shape a cache or a memoised handle would have, and the +0x3c displacement is consistent with a pointer-sized field -- but no record names it and this package claims nothing beyond the word.

What the 8-byte object means, and what the sentinel 0xffffffff means, is not established. The body seeds both words with it, hands the pair to the slot +0x90 dispatch by address, and re-reads whatever came back. A pair of handles initialised to 'unset' and a pair of sentinel-tagged ids are both consistent with the 62 instructions. That the dispatch is given the pair's ADDRESS (so it fills an out-parameter) is machine-fixed; what the pair denotes is not.

Whether the slot +0x04 call is an acquire, a retain, a copy-assign or a validation probe is not established. It sits at index 1 of the resolved handle's own table, it takes the handle in ECX with no stack word, its return value is dead, and the body never releases. 'Acquire' is the reading this package's naming uses and the model test's log strings use, and it is a reading, not a fact.

Which of 0x00612f50's pointer arguments it treats as the out-pointer is not settled from the callee's own frame, and this is reported rather than resolved. The callee reads its first argument as a dword (0x612f7c) and takes its address (0x612f69), and at 0x612fd5 it reads [ESP+0x1c] with its own PUSH EBP -- entry+8, its SECOND argument -- into EBP and stores through it at 0x612fec, while this body reads back the THIRD argument's pointee. Those can both be true only if the callee treats more than one of its pointer arguments as writable, or if the walk of the callee's own frame is wrong. It does not affect this reconstruction: what THIS body does -- pass the address of its third frame word as the third argument, zero that word immediately before the call, and read it back afterwards -- is fixed by this body's own bytes at 0x00642027, 0x00642030 and 0x0064203d, and that is the claim the model asserts.

The 0x0067cb30 global's identity is not established. The callee returns the dword at 0x015fcc70 and the body reads the service out of that object's +0x5c; whether 0x015fcc70 holds a manager, a registry or a singleton pointer is not fixed by anything in this set, and the address is deliberately kept out of the reconstruction's function span.

Whether 0x00613860's key and 0x00612f50's pair are the same kind of identifier is not established. 0x00613860 compares its argument unsigned against an array element's leading word, and 0x00612f50 takes a PAIR and walks elements on a 0x10 stride, so the two callees walk differently-shaped tables. The body passes the receiver's +0x08 to the first and the dispatch's output pair to the second, and nothing here says the two identifiers are related.

The class name SporepediaAssetDataOtdb is INFERRED from vtable co-membership with the nine sibling functions the repository research queue names Sporepedia::cSPAssetDataOTDB::*, and from nothing in this body's own bytes. It is a type name, not a claim about behaviour, and the model asserts nothing that depends on it.

No ordinary caller is named. The record's callers list is empty and the xref export has no inbound call edge; the only inbound references are the seven vtable slots. So the contract of the return value -- whether a caller releases what it is handed, or only inspects it -- is unestablished, and the reconstruction asserts the reference is taken and never released, which is all the body shows.

The RETURN SEMANTICS pass is partly self-referential and a reader should know it. The index record's abi was an empty object before this sidecar existed, so the only canonical return claim the validator could find is the one THIS SIDECAR contributes (observed_original_abi.return_type = "void*"), and the check compares that against the span's own declaration. Before this sidecar existed the check would have compared the evidence pack's prose claim "integral_in_EAX" with the declaration and reported WARN.
